problem: VLM-based navigation and motion planners mostly rely on imitation learning, which needs large labeled expert-trajectory datasets, scales poorly and generalizes badly to long-tail cases. Existing VLM planners also use discrete intermediate representations (cost maps, waypoints, proposals) rather than continuous trajectories optimized end-to-end.
motivation: Robots need both semantic understanding (e.g. finding an 'injured person') and reactive collision-free control. Pretrained VLMs offer the semantics, but adapting them to low-level geometric control without expert labels is unsolved. Depth input is also less sensitive to lighting and texture, which should help sim-to-real transfer.
key_idea: Fine-tune a shared LLaVA-1.6 backbone with swappable LoRA adapters: an RGB adapter for open-vocabulary grounding and a depth adapter with a trajectory head trained via Imperative Learning (differentiable ESDF cost fields) instead of expert trajectories.
insight: Geometric cost supervision alone is enough to adapt a frozen-vision-encoder VLM into a planner reaching over 97% of IPlanner's SPL with about 17.4M trainable parameters. Ablations show that attention pooling in the trajectory head beats mean pooling (Forest Scenario 4 SPL 0.9223 vs 0.6363). Depth input generalizes far better than RGB: RGB fails entirely in Forest Scenario 3 (SPL 0.0) because it mistakes shadows for obstacles, while depth stays at or above 0.89.
method: Shared backbone: LLaVA-v1.6 (CLIP ViT-L/14-336 vision encoder, Vicuna-7B), with the vision encoder frozen and task-specific LoRA modules hot-swapped between two phases.

Target grounding phase: an RGB LoRA adapter outputs a 2D bounding box for an open-vocabulary query; its centroid is back-projected with the depth map and intrinsics K into a 3D goal g = D(u,v)·K^-1[u,v,1]^T.

Depth planning input: the depth map is replicated to 3 channels and split with the Any-Resolution strategy into a 5x3x336x336 tensor; the 3D goal is inserted in the prompt via a reserved <goal> token.
LoRA adaptation: rank 16, alpha 32, on the Q/K/V projections, feed-forward blocks and final FC layer of the LLM; about 12.6M LoRA parameters plus a 4.9M head, roughly 17.4M trainable in total (<1%).

Trajectory head: learnable attention pooling over the hidden states, then an MLP that outputs five 3D keypoints and a collision probability μ; keypoints are spline-interpolated into a trajectory. A μ above 0.5 terminates the run.
Imperative loss: L = α·C_obs + β·C_goal + γ·C_motion + λ·L_fear, using a differentiable ESDF cost map (from iPlanner) and a BCE fear loss for μ, with no expert labels.
Training: 670,325 image-goal pairs from 18 simulation environments, AdamW, lr 1e-5 to 1e-4, 4×A40 GPUs, batch size 12, early stopping.

setting.backbone: LLaVA-v1.6 (CLIP ViT-L/14-336 + Vicuna-7B) with LoRA adapters and a trajectory head
setting.training_data: 670,325 image-goal pairs from 18 simulation environments, trained with cost-field (Imperative Learning) supervision and no expert trajectories; grounding adapter from prior work
setting.observation: Stereo depth image for planning (ZED2i on the real robot), RGB for grounding, plus odometry
setting.action_space: Five predicted 3D waypoints spline-interpolated into a continuous trajectory, tracked by a path-following controller that outputs velocity commands
setting.simulator: Unspecified simulation environments (18 train, 2 unseen test: Indoors and Forest); real world on an AgileX Hunter SE
setting.privileged: ESDF cost map from simulation used for training only; at test time none (ZED2i odometry is used)

numbers_note: No standard VLN/ObjectNav benchmark is used. Simulation results are per-scenario SPL on the authors' own test environments (iPlanner-style), and the baseline numbers (IPlanner) are not repeated here. A depth-vs-RGB ablation is in Table 'Comparison of RGB and Depth Perception (SPL)' (depth 0.9367/0.9226/0.9353/0.8935; RGB 0.8565/0.8816/0.0/0.6362, trained on 12 environments).
results: In unseen simulation the VLM planner reaches SPL 0.9546-0.9631 in Indoors/Forest S1-S3 and 0.9223 in S4, over 97% of the IPlanner baseline (0.9505-0.9827). It keeps larger obstacle margins, which lowers SPL slightly. Zero-shot real-world deployment gives 65.7% overall success (23/35... as reported: 12/20 delivery, 11/15 first-aid) with no body collisions but some wheel contacts.
limitations: About 1 s end-to-end latency forces conservative velocities and limits reactive control among dynamic obstacles.
Slightly below the IPlanner baseline in SPL, and it only plans with a simplified geometric abstraction that ignores robot footprint and kinematics, causing wheel contacts in narrow passages.
Real-world evaluation is small (35 trials) and sensitive to ZED2i odometry drift and imprecise 3D goal projection from bounding boxes on distant objects.
builds_on: Parameter-efficient VLM grounding adapter (Berger et al. 2025)
